positions.commentary: PepsiCo has a partnership with Starbucks to make the CPG version of Frappuccino, which was a huge success.

thesis: Based strictly on the provided claims, this episode highlights two specific strengths of PepsiCo: its dominant market position in sports drinks (specifically Gatorade) and the successful CPG partnership with Starbucks for Frappuccino products. The thesis is limited to these operational advantages without broader strategic or financial arguments.

claims.claim: PepsiCo holds the number one position in sports drinks, which Gatorade does not significantly dent.
claims.quote: Gatorade still has 60%-plus of the market share of sports drinks. Doesn't make a dent in PepsiCo's number one position in sports drinks.

claims.claim: PepsiCo has a partnership with Starbucks to make the CPG version of Frappuccino, which was a huge success.
claims.quote: Ben: That's right. The Pepsi was the bottler that made the CPG version of the Frappuccino. David: Huge success for both companies.

numbers.what: Number of brands Coca-Cola has

numbers.quote: Around 2020 they did a big slimming and went down to about 200.

numbers.quote: They do have 30 brands that do over a billion dollars in revenue.

numbers.what: Number of small brands grown to over a billion in revenue
numbers.quote: Then the remaining 12 of the $30 billion brands that they have were small, and Coke grew them to over a billion in revenue underneath their umbrella.

numbers.what: Total daily servings of beverages Coca-Cola serves
numbers.quote: Coca-Cola serves 2.2 billion servings of their beverages to the world every day.

numbers.what: Coca-Cola Company revenue
numbers.quote: The Coca-Cola company itself does $47 billion in revenue.

numbers.what: Total revenue by the system
numbers.quote: Revenue, $47 billion at Coca-Cola Company out of $175 billion in total revenue by the system.

numbers.what: Number of employees in the system
numbers.quote: But again, if you look at the system, there are 700,000 employees.

numbers.what: Average gross margins
